propertyCopy: Size, tooltip text and badge visibility are properties of the same component, not separate buttons - change them below to check this button's style and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Float Button is a persistent, icon-only action anchored to a fixed corner of the screen, used for a single always-accessible action a user might need regardless of scroll position or context - distinct from an inline Button, which lives within the page's normal content flow. When to Use A persistent utility action - Back to top, Compose new item. A support or help launcher - a customer support chat entry point. A single primary page action that should stay reachable while scrolling - Quick add. When Not to Use Multiple competing floating actions on one screen - pick the single truly persistent action; route the rest through a menu or inline buttons. An action that already exists inline on the page - don't duplicate it as a float - that just adds visual noise. Complex, multi-step actions - a Float Button should trigger something simple or open another surface (Modal, Drawer) - it shouldn't carry the whole flow itself. Best Practices Use exactly one Float Button per screen so it stays meaningfully "the" persistent action. Choose an icon that is universally recognizable without a label (a plus, an upward arrow, a chat bubble). Reserve the badge dot for a real unread/pending count, not decoration. Always pair it with a tooltip, since the control itself carries no visible text. Do and Don't Do + Exactly one floating action, so it reliably means "the persistent thing you can always do here". Don't +✉⚙ A stack of floating buttons covers the content it floats over and turns a clear affordance into a second navigation bar. Accessibility Icon-only, so it needs an explicit aria-label naming the action - there is no visible text to fall back on. The tooltip is a supplementary visual hint, not a substitute for the accessible name. Keeps a full-size touch target even though it's visually compact, meeting WCAG 2.2 target-size guidance.
